note: Our own hiring-manager and HR questions: motivation and logistics (hr), project deep-dives (leadership-ownership) and self-awareness. Questions that assume a current job are dropped for freshers by selection.

questions.title: Why do you want to join this company in particular?
Why are you looking for a change from your current role?
What are your salary expectations, and how did you arrive at them?
What is your notice period, and can it be shortened?
Are you open to relocating to another city for this role?
Are you comfortable working in shifts or with teams in other time zones?
Do you have other offers or interviews in progress?
What do you know about what our team builds?
What would make you leave a job within the first year?
Are you comfortable with a service agreement or training bond?
Would you prefer working on a product, a platform or client projects, and why?
How do you decide between two job offers?
What does a good manager do for you?
Do you have any questions for me about the role or the team?
Why should we hire you over other candidates with similar skills?
How do you plan to grow in your first six months here?
What kind of team culture do you work best in?
Are you open to working in a different technology stack from the one you know?
Walk me through the most significant project on your resume: the problem, your role and the result.
In that project, which design decision would you change now, and why?
What was the hardest trade-off you made in a project you owned?
How did you measure whether your project succeeded?
Tell me about a production issue or demo failure you owned. What happened next?
Which part of your project would break first if usage grew ten times?
What did you build yourself in your project, and what came from libraries or teammates?
How did you test your project, and what bugs did testing catch?
If you had two more weeks on your best project, what would you add?
How did you decide which technologies to use in your project?
Tell me about a time you had to explain your project's progress to a manager or professor.
Describe how you planned and tracked the work in your last project.
What do you expect to find hardest in this role?
Which skill from the job description are you least confident in, and how will you close the gap?
What feedback did your last manager, mentor or professor give you?
How do you handle being given work you find boring?
What would your previous team say they miss about working with you?
How do you react when priorities change suddenly?
